title: Woland: a chronicle of the Russian state press
description:
A daily record of what the Russian state and pro-Kremlin press published since 1 September 2026: every headline, its lead (at most 240 characters), the time and outlet, English machine translations, and the propaganda framings it matched in a documented lexicon, with short snippets as evidence. 23 outlets: the state core (TASS, RIA Novosti, RT, Rossiyskaya Gazeta, Izvestia, Vesti, Zvezda), the official line, the mass press, the foreign-facing English services and a hardline fringe.

Each version is the repository as it stood at a quarterly data release (tag data-YYYY-Q#): the whole archive to that date as JSON Lines (one article per line, filed by Moscow day, under data/articles/), the code that collected it, and the lexicon, glossary and audit it was tagged with. The GitHub release of the same tag also carries that quarter alone as a reproducible archive, its monthly Parquet snapshots, and SHA-256 checksums. Framings are counts of word-pattern matches, not a reading of the articles. Woland does not republish articles; headlines and excerpts remain the property of their publishers.
notes: Code: MIT. Woland's own data (structure, translations, tagging): CC BY 4.0. Headlines and excerpts remain the property of their publishers and are quoted for research and reporting. Several of the outlets fall under the EU broadcasting ban (Council Regulation (EU) 833/2014, art. 2f).
